"title": "Remove old .githooks leftovers and keep eval artifacts 7 days",

"body": "## Why

No pre-commit hook has run since the move to `.vite-hooks` (f774aa2). That is how #143 merged a formatting error that broke main CI and needed #144. Separately, eval run artifacts used GitHub's 90-day default retention and filled the account-wide Actions storage quota (43 artifacts, 1.17 GB).

## Root cause (hooks)

The shared git config still had `core.hooksPath = .githooks`, a folder that no longer exists. The vite-plus `install()` (run by `prepare` → `vp config --no-agent`) does not overwrite another `core.hooksPath`. It prints `core.hooksPath is already set to ".githooks", skipping` and exits 0, so nobody saw it.

The setup itself is fine. `prepare` runs on install and sets `core.hooksPath = .vite-hooks/_`. It also writes the gitignored dispatcher `.vite-hooks/_/` in each checkout. A fresh clone gets it from `pnpm install`. A new T3 worktree gets it from `vp i` in `scripts/setup-worktree.ts`, because a new worktree has no `node_modules`. So no code change is needed there. Only clones that still hold the old `.githooks` value need a one-time local fix:

```sh
git config --unset core.hooksPath && vp config --no-agent
```

I applied that fix to the shared config on this machine and ran `vp config` in the main checkout and every worktree. The main checkout's `node_modules` predates vite-plus, so run `vp i` there before its hook can find `vp staged`.

Proof in this worktree (probes reverted):
- Staged `export const   probe = {a:1,\n    b:2}`. The hook ran `vp check --fix` and committed `export const probe = { a: 1, b: 2 };`.
- Staged a drift in `.agents/skills/comprehende/SKILL.md`. The hook ran `check:skill --staged` and rejected the commit.

## Changes

- Delete `scripts/install-git-hooks.js`, `src/git/hooks.test.ts`, and the stale "Mirrored in scripts/install-git-hooks.js" comment in `src/git/exec.ts`. The test only proved that the old installer sets a relative `.githooks` path that works in linked worktrees. vite-plus now owns that behavior. Nothing else references these files.
- `.github/workflows/eval.yml`: add `retention-days: 7` to `Upload eval run`. `if: always()` stays, because failed runs are the useful ones.

## Review

Comprehende review: https://matemolnar8.github.io/comprehende/pr/145/

## Verification

- `vp check`: pass
- `vp test run src/git/exec.test.ts`: pass
- `tsc --noEmit` (root and `scripts/`): pass
- No eval smoke run: this PR does not touch `skills-next/`, `src/schema/`, or `src/review/`.

"title": "fix(text): classify emoji above U+1F000 by Emoji_Presentation; gate tests/ with clang-format",

"body": "Closes #119.

## Problem

`scripts/clang-format.sh` only checked `src/`, so `tests/*.c` drifted from the style. `vd_emoji_cluster` treated every codepoint at or above U+1F000 as emoji, including Mahjong tiles and text-default symbols like U+1F170.

## Fix

- **Format gate** (`a46f4ed`, kept separate so the reformat doesn't hide the real change): `check` and `format` now cover `tests/`. The nine harnesses are reformatted once (whitespace only). `AGENTS.md` and the `vitadeck-build` skill say so.
- **Emoji classification** (`c2bb5bd`, `e7d27d0`): the Emoji_Presentation table now covers all of Unicode 17 (matching the pinned Twemoji 17.0.3). It is generated from `emoji-data.txt`, and the existing rows below U+1F000 already matched it exactly. The `>= 0x1f000` shortcut is gone, and the sorted table lets the scan stop early, so ASCII exits after one comparison.
- A following skin tone also starts a cluster now. Emoji modifier sequences are fully qualified without U+FE0F (U+1F575 U+1F3FB 🕵🏻), so without this, dropping the shortcut would have broken them. It also fixes U+261D U+1F3FD ☝🏽 below U+1F000, which was already broken but hidden because the harness inserted U+FE0F before the skin tone.

Known edge cases, accepted to stay in scope:
- A non-emoji followed by a skin tone (`a🏻`) now draws only `a`. Fixing that needs an Emoji_Modifier_Base table.
- Minimally-qualified ZWJ sequences with a text-default first codepoint (U+1F3F3 U+200D U+1F308 without U+FE0F) draw as separate images, the same as below U+1F000 today.

## Proof

New `expect_cluster` cases: U+1F000 is not an emoji, U+1F004 is. U+1F170 is not an emoji, but U+1F170 U+FE0F is. A skin tone qualifies a text-default base both above and below U+1F000. The Twemoji round-trip no longer inserts U+FE0F before a skin tone.

The old classifier against the new tests, with all 4011 Twemoji images present:

```
glyph_cache_harness: a Mahjong tile is not an emoji
glyph_cache_harness: a text-style symbol above U+1F000 is not an emoji
glyph_cache_harness: a skin tone makes a text-style symbol below U+1F000 an emoji
glyph_cache_harness: fully qualified text draws its Twemoji image   (x36, e.g. 261d-1f3fb.png)
```

New classifier: `glyph_cache_harness: ok`.

```
$ ./scripts/clang-format.sh check   # now includes tests/
$ echo $?
0
```

Checks: `scripts/agent-check.sh fast` and `host` pass (15/15 CTest). The Vita Docker build (`vitadeck.vpk`) passes. No rendering of existing content changes, so I skipped the smoke tier. CI has no C format step (only `agent-check.sh` runs it); adding one is left out of scope.

"title": "[Claude] Unhandled promise rejections in Deck Apps fail silently",

"body": "## Problem
PR #66 (#44) routes render errors, handler errors, timer errors and module-eval errors to the Deck App Failure Screen, but an unhandled promise rejection (e.g. a `fetch` chain without a `catch`) is still swallowed. QuickJS only reports these through `JS_SetHostPromiseRejectionTracker`, which `src/core/js_runtime.c` never installs.

## Fix
Install a rejection tracker at runtime start that logs the reason and reports it through the same path as `nativeReportDeckAppError` (or just logs it, if we prefer not to fail the app on a rejection; decide and document in `CONTEXT.md`). Cover with a scenario in the harness that loads a Deck App whose effect rejects a promise.

Posted by Claude Code [claude-fable-5-1]",
"title": "[Claude] Data race on stb_ds global hash seed between JS and main threads",

"body": "## Problem
ThreadSanitizer (run manually while building the #58 harnesses, PR #77) reports a race on stb_ds's global `stbds_hash_seed`: both the JS thread and the main thread write it when they create hash maps. Lock-free writes to a shared seed are undefined behaviour and can make two threads hash the same key differently.

## Fix
Call `stbds_rand_seed` (or otherwise initialise the seed) once at startup before any thread starts, and make sure no later code path re-seeds. Consider wiring the TSan run into the sanitized CI step once it is clean.

Posted by Claude Code [claude-fable-5-1]",
"title": "fix(runtime): report unhandled rejections, stop stb_ds seed race, log dropped events",

"body": "## Problem

An unhandled promise rejection in a Deck App (e.g. a `fetch` chain without a `catch`) was swallowed silently, because the JS thread never installed QuickJS's rejection tracker (#69). Separately, TSan found the JS and main threads both writing stb_ds's global `stbds_hash_seed` (#78).

## Fix

- **Rejections (#69):** `src/core/js_runtime.c` installs `JS_SetHostPromiseRejectionTracker`. Rejections without a handler are held until the microtask queue drains. If a handler attaches in the meantime (QuickJS calls the tracker again with `is_handled` true), the rejection is dropped. Anything still pending is reported through the same path as other uncaught errors and shows the Deck App Failure Screen. `CONTEXT.md` documents this choice. `js_limits_harness` gains three scenarios: an unhandled rejection at boot, one inside a timer, and a rejection whose `catch` attaches in a later microtask, which must not fail the app.
- **Hash seed (#78):** seeding once at startup would not fix the race. stb_ds advances the global seed with an LCG every time any thread creates a new hash map, so every map creation is a write. The vendored `stb_ds.h` now only reads the seed (one hunk, marked `VitaDeck:`). Each table already keeps its own seed, so hashing is unchanged per table.
- `event_queue_push` now logs a `TraceLog` warning when it drops an event on a full queue. Drop-newest behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification

- `fast` on macOS. `tsc` only passes after `pnpm --dir js build`, which was already true before this change.
- `host` + smoke (all 12 CTest harnesses) in the Linux smoke Docker image, both plain and with `VITADECK_SANITIZE=address,undefined`.
- Vita build in the Vitasdk Docker image.
- One manual TSan run in Docker (not wired into CI). `snapshot_swap_harness` and `event_queue_harness` were clean. `js_limits_harness` reports no stb_ds race; the races it does report are on the existing `volatile` `failed`/`failure_message` fields of `VdJsRuntime`, which are out of scope here.

"title": "[Claude] Track and minimise local patches to vendored code (stb_ds seed fix)",

"body": "## Problem
PR #81 fixed the stb_ds hash seed race (#78) by editing `vendor/stb_ds.h` (removing the per-table LCG advance of the global seed). Máté approved it but does not want vendored code modified: patched vendor files drift from upstream and make updates risky. `vendor/jimp.h` is already locally patched (ADR 0003), so there are now two.

## Proposal
1. Record every local vendor patch in one place (e.g. `vendor/PATCHES.md` with the upstream version, the diff summary and the reason) so an upgrade can replay them. Add the two existing ones.
2. For stb_ds specifically, check whether the fix can live in `src/` instead: e.g. a build-time define upstream already supports, or creating all hash maps on one thread before the JS thread starts. If neither works, propose the change upstream to nothings/stb and keep the local patch marked `VitaDeck:` as it is now.

"title": "[Claude] upload_vita does not push assets/emoji, so a fresh VPK install is needed before emoji show",

"body": "## Problem
#91 adds Twemoji PNGs under the app's `assets/emoji`, shipped inside the VPK. The `upload_vita` CMake target (eboot over FTP for quick iteration) only uploads the binary, so after a code-only upload a device without a prior full VPK install renders emoji as missing. Noted by the #91 agent.

## Fix
Make `upload_vita` also sync the assets directory (or document that the VPK must be installed once after asset changes) and mention it in the `vitadeck-build` skill.

Posted by Claude Code [claude-fable-5-1]",
"title": "chore: record vendored patches; upload_vita syncs emoji assets",

"body": "Vendored code had untracked local patches (#87), and `upload_vita` never sent `assets/emoji`, so a Vita without a full VPK install showed no emoji after a code-only upload (#93).

## Vendor patches (#87)
`vendor/PATCHES.md` now lists every local change to vendored code, with the upstream commit, a summary of the diff and why it exists, and how to replay it on upgrade. An audit against upstream found three:
- `stb_ds.h`: the seed race fix from #81
- `jimp/jimp.h`: two fixes for Vita GCC warnings (ADR 0003)
- `quickjs` submodule: the fork's single "Vita" commit on top of bellard/quickjs `e5fd391`, which adds `__vita__` platform guards

`arena.h`, `raylib.h` and `stb_truetype.h` match upstream byte for byte. `jimp/README.md` and ADR 0003 now point to `PATCHES.md` so the patches are described in one place.

**The stb_ds patch stays.** No `STBDS_*` option turns off the per-table seed update. Seeding once at startup doesn't help either, because every later table creation writes the seed again. Removing the patch would also require all hash maps to be created on one thread, but the JS thread builds a new instance registry on every swap while the main thread creates the scroll and glyph maps lazily. I checked this under TSan with `snapshot_swap_harness` in the Linux smoke image (`-DVITADECK_SANITIZE=thread`). With the upstream header, TSan reports the race in `stbds_make_hash_index` between `deep_copy_instance` and `scroll.c`'s `ensure_map`. With the patched header it runs clean. The patch is still marked `VitaDeck:`, and I restored upstream's trailing newline so the diff contains only the marked change.

## upload_vita syncs emoji (#93)
At configure time CMake writes `upload_emoji.curl`, a curl config that lists every PNG. `upload_vita` runs it in one curl process over one FTP connection and shows an `n/4009` progress counter. A stamp per build directory and Vita IP means the step runs again only when the images change, so normal iterations stay fast. Delete the stamp to force a re-upload. The `vitadeck-build` skill documents this. If no emoji were downloaded (offline configure), the step is skipped.

## Verification
- `scripts/agent-check.sh fast` passed (pnpm 10.28.2).
- Vita Docker build passed and produced `vitadeck.vpk`.
- `upload_vita` ran against a local FTP stub (pyftpdlib on 1337) on the same Docker network, with `PSVITAIP` pointing at the stub. All 4009 PNGs arrived byte-identical, and a second run skipped the emoji step. The emoji step took about 25 s against the stub; expect longer over Vita Wi-Fi. Not tested on hardware.
- No `src/` C changes, so I skipped the `host` tier.

No pre-commit hook has run since the move to `.vite-hooks` (f774aa2). That is how #143 merged a formatting error that broke main CI and needed #144. Separately, eval run artifacts used GitHub's 90-day default retention and filled the account-wide Actions storage quota (43 artifacts, 1.17 GB).

## Root cause (hooks)

The shared git config still had `core.hooksPath = .githooks`, a folder that no longer exists. The vite-plus `install()` (run by `prepare` → `vp config --no-agent`) does not overwrite another `core.hooksPath`. It prints `core.hooksPath is already set to ".githooks", skipping` and exits 0, so nobody saw it.

The setup itself is fine. `prepare` runs on install and sets `core.hooksPath = .vite-hooks/_`. It also writes the gitignored dispatcher `.vite-hooks/_/` in each checkout. A fresh clone gets it from `pnpm install`. A new T3 worktree gets it from `vp i` in `scripts/setup-worktree.ts`, because a new worktree has no `node_modules`. So no code change is needed there. Only clones that still hold the old `.githooks` value need a one-time local fix:

```sh
git config --unset core.hooksPath && vp config --no-agent
```

I applied that fix to the shared config on this machine and ran `vp config` in the main checkout and every worktree. The main checkout's `node_modules` predates vite-plus, so run `vp i` there before its hook can find `vp staged`.

Proof in this worktree (probes reverted):
- Staged `export const   probe = {a:1,\n    b:2}`. The hook ran `vp check --fix` and committed `export const probe = { a: 1, b: 2 };`.
- Staged a drift in `.agents/skills/comprehende/SKILL.md`. The hook ran `check:skill --staged` and rejected the commit.

## Changes

- Delete `scripts/install-git-hooks.js`, `src/git/hooks.test.ts`, and the stale "Mirrored in scripts/install-git-hooks.js" comment in `src/git/exec.ts`. The test only proved that the old installer sets a relative `.githooks` path that works in linked worktrees. vite-plus now owns that behavior. Nothing else references these files.
- `.github/workflows/eval.yml`: add `retention-days: 7` to `Upload eval run`. `if: always()` stays, because failed runs are the useful ones.

"body": "## Why

No pre-commit hook has run since the move to `.vite-hooks` (f774aa2). That is how #143 merged a formatting error that broke main CI and needed #144. Separately, eval run artifacts used GitHub's 90-day default retention and filled the account-wide Actions storage quota (43 artifacts, 1.17 GB).

## Root cause (hooks)

The shared git config still had `core.hooksPath = .githooks`, a folder that no longer exists. The vite-plus `install()` (run by `prepare` → `vp config --no-agent`) does not overwrite another `core.hooksPath`. It prints `core.hooksPath is already set to ".githooks", skipping` and exits 0, so nobody saw it.

The setup itself is fine. `prepare` runs on install and sets `core.hooksPath = .vite-hooks/_`. It also writes the gitignored dispatcher `.vite-hooks/_/` in each checkout. A fresh clone gets it from `pnpm install`. A new T3 worktree gets it from `vp i` in `scripts/setup-worktree.ts`, because a new worktree has no `node_modules`. So no code change is needed there. Only clones that still hold the old `.githooks` value need a one-time local fix:

```sh
git config --unset core.hooksPath && vp config --no-agent
```

I applied that fix to the shared config on this machine and ran `vp config` in the main checkout and every worktree. The main checkout's `node_modules` predates vite-plus, so run `vp i` there before its hook can find `vp staged`.

Proof in this worktree (probes reverted):
- Staged `export const   probe = {a:1,\n    b:2}`. The hook ran `vp check --fix` and committed `export const probe = { a: 1, b: 2 };`.
- Staged a drift in `.agents/skills/comprehende/SKILL.md`. The hook ran `check:skill --staged` and rejected the commit.

## Changes

- Delete `scripts/install-git-hooks.js`, `src/git/hooks.test.ts`, and the stale "Mirrored in scripts/install-git-hooks.js" comment in `src/git/exec.ts`. The test only proved that the old installer sets a relative `.githooks` path that works in linked worktrees. vite-plus now owns that behavior. Nothing else references these files.
- `.github/workflows/eval.yml`: add `retention-days: 7` to `Upload eval run`. `if: always()` stays, because failed runs are the useful ones.

## Review

Comprehende review: https://matemolnar8.github.io/comprehende/pr/145/

## Verification

- `vp check`: pass
- `vp test run src/git/exec.test.ts`: pass
- `tsc --noEmit` (root and `scripts/`): pass
- No eval smoke run: this PR does not touch `skills-next/`, `src/schema/`, or `src/review/`.

Posted by Claude [claude-opus-5-5]

lines.text: "title": "Agent tooling: Pages publish waits for its deploy, plus check:changed and worktree setup",

"body": "A retro of the last 10 agent sessions found agents losing time on the same repo tooling gaps: Pages deploys that 404 for minutes after a "successful" publish, worktrees without `node_modules`/`.env`, hand-built `vp check` file lists that break in zsh, and AGENTS.md pointers that lead to the wrong files or commands.

- **Pages publish waits for its deploy.** `scripts/pages-review.ts publish` now waits for the `pages-build-deployment` run whose `head_sha` is the pushed `gh-pages` commit, reruns it once if it fails (the usual "in progress deployment" lock), and prints `deploy <state>` after the URL. `--no-wait` skips it. The pages skill now says a 404 means the deploy is running or failed, what to do on a lasting lock, and to publish once per PR with screenshots inside the export folder.
- **`pnpm check:changed`** runs `vp check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern` on files changed against the merge-base with `origin/main` plus untracked files. Markdown-only lists no longer fail with "No files found to lint". Extra flags pass through (`--fix`).
- **`node scripts/setup-worktree.ts`** works outside T3: without `T3CODE_PROJECT_ROOT`, it links `.env` from the main checkout (first `git worktree list` entry).
- **AGENTS.md** points to `pnpm ui:screenshots`, `src/api/`, real `src/review/` file names, how to find every layer for a new review field, `pnpm generate:schema` / `pnpm sync:skill` before commit, the `skills-next` + local-CLI PR review flow, and `--cli-login`.

Comprehende review: https://matemolnar8.github.io/comprehende/pr/182/ (published with the new wait: `deploy success` after 59 s)

Verified: `vp test run scripts/pages-review.test.ts scripts/setup-worktree.test.ts` (16 passed), `pnpm check:changed` clean, `node scripts/setup-worktree.ts` without the env var in this worktree linked `.env`. No smoke eval: nothing under `skills-next/comprehende/`, `src/schema/`, or `src/review/` changed.

"body": "## Problem
Two small things noted by the merge-gate review of #114:
1. `scripts/clang-format.sh` only checks `src/`, so `tests/*.c` has lines over 120 columns and drifts from the style. Either gate `tests/` too (and reformat once) or document that tests are unformatted.
2. `src/ui/glyph_cache.c` treats every codepoint at or above U+1F000 as emoji. That includes non-emoji such as Mahjong tiles and text-default-presentation symbols like U+1F170. Harmless today because the first-codepoint fallback draws them from a font when Twemoji has no file, but the classification should use the Emoji property ranges above U+1F000 the same way the new table does below it.

Posted by Claude Code [claude-fable-5-1]",

+  "body": "Closes #119.

## Problem

`scripts/clang-format.sh` only checked `src/`, so `tests/*.c` drifted from the style. `vd_emoji_cluster` treated every codepoint at or above U+1F000 as emoji, including Mahjong tiles and text-default symbols like U+1F170.

## Fix

- **Format gate** (`a46f4ed`, kept separate so the reformat doesn't hide the real change): `check` and `format` now cover `tests/`. The nine harnesses are reformatted once (whitespace only). `AGENTS.md` and the `vitadeck-build` skill say so.
- **Emoji classification** (`c2bb5bd`, `e7d27d0`): the Emoji_Presentation table now covers all of Unicode 17 (matching the pinned Twemoji 17.0.3). It is generated from `emoji-data.txt`, and the existing rows below U+1F000 already matched it exactly. The `>= 0x1f000` shortcut is gone, and the sorted table lets the scan stop early, so ASCII exits after one comparison.
- A following skin tone also starts a cluster now. Emoji modifier sequences are fully qualified without U+FE0F (U+1F575 U+1F3FB 🕵🏻), so without this, dropping the shortcut would have broken them. It also fixes U+261D U+1F3FD ☝🏽 below U+1F000, which was already broken but hidden because the harness inserted U+FE0F before the skin tone.

Known edge cases, accepted to stay in scope:
- A non-emoji followed by a skin tone (`a🏻`) now draws only `a`. Fixing that needs an Emoji_Modifier_Base table.
- Minimally-qualified ZWJ sequences with a text-default first codepoint (U+1F3F3 U+200D U+1F308 without U+FE0F) draw as separate images, the same as below U+1F000 today.

## Proof

New `expect_cluster` cases: U+1F000 is not an emoji, U+1F004 is. U+1F170 is not an emoji, but U+1F170 U+FE0F is. A skin tone qualifies a text-default base both above and below U+1F000. The Twemoji round-trip no longer inserts U+FE0F before a skin tone.

The old classifier against the new tests, with all 4011 Twemoji images present:

```
glyph_cache_harness: a Mahjong tile is not an emoji
glyph_cache_harness: a text-style symbol above U+1F000 is not an emoji
glyph_cache_harness: a skin tone makes a text-style symbol below U+1F000 an emoji
glyph_cache_harness: fully qualified text draws its Twemoji image   (x36, e.g. 261d-1f3fb.png)
```

New classifier: `glyph_cache_harness: ok`.

```
$ ./scripts/clang-format.sh check   # now includes tests/
$ echo $?
0
```

Checks: `scripts/agent-check.sh fast` and `host` pass (15/15 CTest). The Vita Docker build (`vitadeck.vpk`) passes. No rendering of existing content changes, so I skipped the smoke tier. CI has no C format step (only `agent-check.sh` runs it); adding one is left out of scope.

"body": "A retro of the last 10 agent sessions (ubuntu-pc and the MacBook Pro) found that agents find code fine; the time goes on stale or missing know-how. In most sessions an agent worked out from scratch how to drive and record the host window, because the manual-testing skill points at tmux and `computerUse`, which those sessions didn't have. Docker smoke runs left root-owned SDK output that broke the next `pnpm build`. Adding a demo section silently left `ROUNDS` and the bench keys stale. Refreshing a PR review deleted its screenshots. Device lessons (one FTP connection per upload, Vita3K won't render headless on ubuntu-pc) lived only in one machine's agent memory.

- `scripts/gui-drive.sh` (`key`, `click`, `shot`, `rect`) drives the window on Linux X11 or Xvfb (xdotool and ffmpeg, with the down/up events GLFW needs) and on macOS (a Swift CGEvent helper). lines.text: "title": "[Claude] Data race on stb_ds global hash seed between JS and main threads",

"body": "## Problem
ThreadSanitizer (run manually while building the #58 harnesses, PR #77) reports a race on stb_ds's global `stbds_hash_seed`: both the JS thread and the main thread write it when they create hash maps. Lock-free writes to a shared seed are undefined behaviour and can make two threads hash the same key differently.

## Fix
Call `stbds_rand_seed` (or otherwise initialise the seed) once at startup before any thread starts, and make sure no later code path re-seeds. Consider wiring the TSan run into the sanitized CI step once it is clean.

Posted by Claude Code [claude-fable-5-1]",
